title: Assessing the Wnt-reactivity of cytonemes of mouse embryonic stem cells using a bioengineering approach
protocol: Optional: Add 2 μM IWP2 to the media of one well of TSCs 24 h before use.
Aspirate culture media from one well of TSCs.
Rinse the TSCs once with PBS.
Add 0.5 mL of 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA to the plate.
Incubate for less than 4 minutes at 37°C and 5% CO2 until cells are detached.
Resuspend the cells with 2 mL TSC media using a 5 mL serological pipette.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Add 2 μM IWP2 to the media for IWP2-treated TSCs.
Centrifuge the cells at 1.2 × 10^3 rcf for 4 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant, avoiding contact with the pelleted cells.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of TSC media by pipetting up and down.
Transfer the cell suspension to a clean 6-well plate.
Incubate for approximately 15 minutes at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Carefully remove the supernatant containing TSCs without disturbing attached MEFs.
Pellet cells by centrifugation at 1.2 × 10^3 rcf for 4 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant, avoiding contact with the pelleted cells.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of TSC media briefly pipetting up and down.
Estimate the concentration of cell clusters using a glass hemocytometer.
Aspirate culture media from a well of ESCs or primed ESCs stably expressing Ftractin-mRuby3.
Rinse cells once with PBS.
Add 0.5 mL 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA and return the plate to the incubator.
Incubate for less than 4 min at 37°C, 5% CO2 until cells are detached.
Resuspend cells in 2 mL ESC basal media using a 5 mL serological pipette.
Transfer cell suspension to a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Pellet cells by centrifugation at 1.2 × 10^3 rcf for 4 min at room temperature.
Aspirate supernatant, carefully avoiding the pelleted cells.
Resuspend pelleted cells in 1 mL ESC basal media by repeatedly pipetting the whole volume up and down.
Estimate cell concentration using a glass hemocytometer.
Optimize cell density for ESC/primed ESC and TSCs interactions.
Gently mix cells and transfer 200 μl of the mixture to one well of a black-walled, clear-bottomed TC-treated 96-well plate.
Incubate the plate at 37°C in an incubator with 5% CO2 for 1 hour to allow cell attachment.
Transfer cells to a pre-warmed polystyrene box for transport between incubator and microscope (optional).
Pre-stabilize the incubation box of the spinning disk microscope at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Place the imaging 96-well plate in the motorized stage of the microscope.
Select the 20×/0.75 objective for imaging.
Perform Kohler illumination adjustment of the transmitted light.
Choose representative positions in which ESCs or primed ESCs and TSCs are closely located, but not contacting.
Use the mRuby3 channel to visualize ESCs or primed ESCs and the thin structures in their cytonemes.
Use the GFP channel to localize TSCs.
Choose approximately 20 positions per well.
Adjust laser intensities and exposure times to be as low as possible to avoid phototoxicity.
Set up 3 z-positions to sample the full volume of the cell, approximately 3–5 μm apart.
Center the Z-stack to the position with a higher resolution of the cytonemes.
Set up the time-lapse imaging protocol: image each position every 10 minutes for 12 hours using brightfield, mRuby3 (RFP) and GFP channels.
Optional: Image a one-cycle loop to check that the setup is correct.
Image ESC/primed ESC-TSC interaction overnight.
Run automated imaging overnight (∼12 h).
Aspirate culture media from a 6-well plate culture of ESCs or primed ESCs stably expressing Ftractin-mRuby3.
Rinse the cells once with PBS.
Add 0.5 ml of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA to the wells.
Return the plate to the incubator for ∼4 minutes at 37°C, 5% CO2 until cells are detached.
Do not incubate cells with 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA for longer than 5 minutes.
Resuspend cells in 2 mL of ESC basal media using a 5 mL serological pipette.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 1.2 × 10^3 rcf for 4 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully without disturbing the pelleted cells.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of ESC basal media by pipetting up and down repeatedly.
Estimate cell concentration using a glass hemocytometer.
Dilute ESCs or primed ESCs to 3,000 cells per 100 μL in ESC basal media.
Add 0.3 μg of Wnt3a-beads or control beads to the cell suspension for each well required.
Mix ESC basal media with the cell and bead mixture to achieve a final concentration of 3,000 cells and 0.3 μg beads per 200 μL.
Transfer 200 μL of the mix to the wells of a black-walled, clear-bottomed TC-treated, 96-well plate.
Return to the incubator and incubate for 1 h at 37°C, 5% CO2 to allow cell attachment.
Transfer cells to a pre-warmed polystyrene box for transport to the microscope.
Pre-stabilize the incubation box of the spinning disk microscope at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Place the cell-containing 96-well plate in the motorized stage.
Select the 20×/0.75 objective (or equivalent).
Perform Kohler illumination adjustment of the transmitted light following standard procedures.
Choose representative positions in which ESCs and Wnt-beads or control-beads are closely located, but not already contacting.
Use the mRuby3 channel to visualize ESCs or primed ESCs and the thin structures in their cytonemes.
Adjust laser intensities and exposure times to be as low as possible to avoid phototoxicity (e.g., 30 ms for brightfield, 200 ms and 20% laser power for RFP-561 nm laser with 4x binning).
Set up 3 z-positions covering the full volume of the cell (approximately 3–5 μm apart).
Center the Z-stack to the position with better resolution of the cytonemes.
Set up the time-lapse imaging protocol.
Image each position every 10 minutes, for 12 hours, for brightfield and mRuby3 (RFP channel).
Choose enough positions to achieve a good representation of the ESC-TSC dynamics throughout the well but few enough so a cycle of imaging can be performed within the 10-minute interval.
Image ESC/primed ESC-bead interactions for 12 hours using the automated imaging protocol.
Perform reactivity analysis in the images obtained.
Quantify cytoneme reactivity to sources of Wnt (Wnt3a-beads or TSCs) over a period of 3-6 hours.
Process raw data in Excel.
Represent and statistically analyze processed data in Prism version 8 or later.
Identify ESCs or primed ESCs that interact with a bead or TSC via a cytoneme using the F-tractin-mRuby3 signal.
Crop cells of interest from the larger field of view for ease of analysis and minimizing storage requirements.

Exclude apoptotic/non-adherent cells, non-cytoneme-mediated interactions resulting from cell or bead movement, and interactions through cytonemes already in contact with a bead or TSC at the start of video from the analysis.
Observe the interaction between the ESC/primed ESC and the source of Wnt.
Record values for all measurements listed below in an Excel sheet, one row per interaction analyzed.
Measure and register the initial distance between the ESC/primed ESC and the TSC using the "Line" tool in Fiji.
Record the frame in which the initial interaction occurs.
Measure the distance between the center of the ESC/primed ESC and the source of Wnt at the time of interaction.
Determine if contact is maintained, resulting in bead recruitment towards the soma or ESC/primed ESC-TSC pairing.
Categorize the interaction as a "Reactive interaction" if contact is maintained.
Record the frame where recruitment/pairing occurs.
Categorize the interaction as a "Non-reactive interaction" if no subsequent recruitment/pairing occurs.
Use the “Line” tool to measure the distance between ESC/primed ESC and Wnt source in frames after contact.
Measure the distance 3 frames (30 min) after contact for ESC/primed ESC-Wnt-bead interaction.
Measure the distance 5 frames (50 min) after contact for ESC/primed ESC-TSC pairing.
Register the time of loss of contact if ESC/primed ESC-Wnt source contact is lost.
Register the time until the end of the video if contact is maintained until then.
Analyze each interaction, aiming to analyze at least 30 cells from each experiment.
Pool cells from ≥ 3 independent experiments for post-analysis.
Calculate the “Change in distance after contact” by subtracting the “Distance at contact” from the “Distance at contact+30”.
For “Reactive interactions”, calculate the “Time of Reaction” by subtracting the “Time of contact” from the “Time of pairing”.
Calculate the “Time of Retention” by subtracting the “Time of contact” from the “Time of loss of contact”.
Convert frame-based measurement values to minutes, with 1 frame equal to 10 minutes.
Repeat analysis and post-analysis for all conditions examined.
Use Prism (GraphPad) for data presentation and comparison between conditions.
Aspirate culture media from GCaMP6s-expressing ESCs or primed ESCs in a 6-well plate.
Rinse cells once with PBS.
Add 0.5 mL of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA to the cells and return the plate to the incubator.
Incubate for approximately 4 minutes at 37°C, 5% CO2 until cells are detached.
Resuspend the cells using 2 mL of ESC basal media with a 5 mL serological pipette.
Transfer cell suspension to a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Pellet cells by centrifugation at 1.2 × 10^3 rcf for 4 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant, carefully avoiding the pelleted cells.
Resuspend the pelleted cells in 1 mL of ESC basal media by repeatedly pipetting up and down.
Estimate the concentration of cells in the suspension using a glass hemocytometer.
Dilute ESCs or primed ESCs to 7,000 cells per 250 μL in ESC basal media.
Transfer the cell mixture to a well of an ibiTreat μ-Slide 8 well slide.
Incubate for 4–6 h at 37°C and 5% CO2 until cells are attached and generate cytonemes.
Pre-stabilize the incubation box of the spinning disk microscope at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Transfer cells to a pre-warmed polystyrene box if transferring to the microscope is necessary.
Place the cell-containing slide in the motorized stage.
Select the 20×/0.75 objective or an equivalent one.
Perform Kohler illumination adjustment of the transmitted light following standard procedures.
Add Wnt3a-beads (or control-beads, such as inactivated Wnt3a-beads, Wnt5a-beads, or BSA-beads) to the slide.
Prepare a tube with 25 μL ESC basal media.
Transfer 1 μg Wnt3a-beads to the tube containing media and mix.
Triturate stock Wnt3a-bead solution by pipetting up and down for >100 times using a ∼100 μL volume.
Add the diluted Wnt3a-bead solution to the well of GCaMP6s-expressing ESCs or primed ESCs, dropwise.
Incubate for ∼15 min to allow the Wnt3a-beads to reach the bottom of the well.
Choose a cell that is contacting a Wnt3a-bead with a cytoneme using brightfield imaging.
Visualize GCaMP6s-expressing ESCs or primed ESCs and find an optimal z-plane for stable imaging of the interaction.
Adjust laser intensities and exposure times to be as low as possible to avoid phototoxicity.
Set up the time-lapse imaging protocol: one image every 5 s, for 20 min.
Capture images for brightfield and GCaMP6s (GFP channel) at every loop.
Choose another cell/position and repeat imaging.
Use the GCaMP6s signal to identify single ESCs or primed ESCs that contact Wnt-bead with a cytoneme.
Crop cells of interest from the larger field of view for ease of analysis and minimizing storage requirements.
Exclude interactions resulting from cell motility or bead movement (i.e., non-cytoneme mediated interactions) from the analysis.
Exclude apoptotic/non-adherent cells from the analysis.
View the GCaMP6s signal using a high-contrast LUT, such as ‘Fire’ in ImageJ.
Identify Ca2+ transients qualitatively as a sharp increase in GCaMP6s signal over the course of <30 s.
Distinguish cytoneme-localized transients from whole-cell transients or those emanating from the cell-soma manually.
Record the start time point of each localized transient when the GCaMP6s signal increases.
Record the end time point of each localized transient when the GCaMP6s signal returns to basal level.
Calculate the duration of each localized transient using the recorded start and end time points.
Calculate the mean duration of all transients occurring within each cell.
Count the number of localized transients per cell.
